- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast slope to avoid underreaction.  
- When true outcome shows sharp spikes or drops, model often over- or under-anticipates — adjust forecast by 1–2 days lag to align with actual volatility.  
- If model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days), apply downward bias correction by 3–5% to prevent overshoot.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and forecast is flat, check for mean reversion — if true outcome deviates > 5% from recent mean, adjust forecast toward historical average.  
- For periods with high volatility (e.g., 2022-04-11 to 2022-04-21), reduce forecast smoothness — allow ±2% deviation from prior 7-day average to capture sudden shifts.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated positive spikes, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast by 10–15% in the 10–15 day window following such events.
